items.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He's the guy that took my place for a while. Dizzy took a singer with him. So Bernard Igner, he was singing with Dizzy.

ctx.x: Uh-huh (affirmative). So that's when you were with the quintet.

Yeah. And Bernard Igner (phonetic sp.). You know that song [sings] everything much change. Nothing [stops singing] – He's the gentleman that wrote that song. He's the guy that took my place for a while. Dizzy took a singer with him. So Bernard Igner, he was singing with Dizzy. And then when I got better I went back. You know. They said, "Moody. It doesn't make any difference. You just play what you can play and what you can." Cause I could play like – (scatting – gets louder and then fades out) You know. It would…
So you still kept working across that time even though you were ill.
